message_text: Hello, I mistakenly sent GHS 500 to your number instead of my sister. Please send it back to 024XXXXXXX. God bless you.
grounding_note: GNA reports a syndicate posing as mistaken senders to defraud victims of GHS 130,000 [citation:1]. ScamEncyclopedia documents this exact pattern: fake deposit followed by reversal request [citation:3].

message_text: Your MoMo account has been blocked due to suspicious activity. Call MTN customer care on 059XXXXXXX to reactivate. Do not ignore.
grounding_note: Cybersecurity expert David Gyedu describes fraudsters calling from ordinary numbers claiming accounts are blocked and impersonating MTN/Telecel [citation:2]. ScamEncyclopedia notes callers walk victims through keypad steps that approve transfers [citation:3].

message_text: Congratulations! Your number has won GHS 10,000 in the MTN Mega Promo. Send your MoMo PIN to 024XXXXXXX to claim your prize now.
grounding_note: Expert notes fake prize messages have been a traditional tactic, though fraudsters are shifting to brand impersonation [citation:2]. PIN request is never legitimate per multiple guides [citation:3][citation:14].

message_text: Papa, I am in trouble. I had an accident and I need GHS 300 urgently for hospital. Please send to this number. I will explain later. — Kojo
grounding_note: Advance fee fraud advisories describe scammers posing as long-lost relatives or using urgency to compel payment [citation:7]. Romance scam reporting shows Ghanaians exploit emotional emergencies for wire transfers [citation:9].

message_text: Dear customer, your DStv subscription upgrade requires verification. Click this link and enter your MoMo PIN to complete. Offer expires in 10 minutes.
grounding_note: Actress Joselyn Dumas lost funds after a fake DStv agent sent links and extracted her PIN under urgency [citation:4][citation:15]. GBC reports this as part of rising MoMo fraud via brand impersonation [citation:4].

message_text: Hello, I am an MTN customer care officer. We detected an unauthorized transaction on your account. Please read me the OTP you just received so I can block the transaction.
grounding_note: ScamEncyclopedia warns providers never ask for PIN or OTP; scammers call claiming to reverse transactions or unblock accounts [citation:3][citation:14]. LinkedIn analysis describes the call that follows SMS panic as the theft moment [citation:6].

message_text: Your SIM will be deactivated today. To keep your number, confirm your Ghana Card number and date of birth by replying to this message.
grounding_note: SIM swap guide notes fraudsters gather national ID and date of birth to request replacement SIMs; red flag includes requests to confirm ID details over the phone [citation:5].

message_text: Eii, my brother! I've mistakenly sent you GHS 200. Abeg send it back make I no lose am. This is my number: 055XXXXXXX. Thank you.
grounding_note: Same pattern as row 1, rendered in Ghanaian English/Twi code-mixing style. GNA case involved GHS 130,000 loss via this method [citation:1]. The code-mixing reflects typical Ghanaian informal communication.

message_text: Your MTN MoMo transaction of GHS 50.00 to 024XXXXXXX has been completed. Your new balance is GHS 120.00. Transaction ID: 1234567890. Thank you.
grounding_note: Analyst notes genuine MTN messages come from alphanumeric "MobileMoney" sender, have consistent formatting, 10-digit transaction ID, and match actual balance [citation:6][citation:10].

message_text: Chale, I dey come your side later. Make we talk about the job thing. I go call you when I reach.
grounding_note: Benign Ghanaian English/Twi mixed conversational message. No fraud indicators. Demonstrates need to distinguish casual code-mixed chat from fraud scripts.

message_text: URGENT: Your account will be frozen. Click http://mtn-gh-verify.xyz to confirm your details within 24 hours or lose access permanently.
grounding_note: Expert warns of malware and phishing links exploiting national events; advises use official websites only [citation:2]. ScamEncyclopedia documents fake provider calls/links [citation:3].

message_text: You have received GHS 1,500.00 from 024XXXXXXX. Reference: Cash In. Your new balance is GHS 1,500.00. Transaction ID: 9876543210.
grounding_note: LinkedIn forensic analysis dissects a three-SMS script: fake cash-in, fake reversal, fake block—all to create panic before the call where PIN is stolen [citation:6]. Formatting inconsistencies (GHS 920.00 vs GHS920.0) betray human typing.

message_text: We are recruiting part-time workers. Earn GHS 500 daily liking posts on social media. WhatsApp 055XXXXXXX to start immediately. No experience needed.
grounding_note: CSA reports 352 job scam cases in first half 2026 with GHS 3.4 million losses; scammers pose as recruiters for digital tasks and direct victims to WhatsApp [citation:8].

message_text: Hello dear, I saw your profile and I feel a connection. I am a soldier deployed overseas. I need your help to receive a package; I will pay you back. Please send your number and address.
grounding_note: FBI case: Ghanaian ring defrauded Americans of over $100 million via romance scams posing as partners in distress [citation:9]. CSA warns of long-lost relatives and wealthy personas [citation:7].

message_text: MTN Mobile Money: Your PIN has been changed successfully. If you did not initiate this, call 0244300000 immediately.
grounding_note: This could be genuine (MTN does send security alerts) or a precursor to a callback scam where the victim calls a spoofed number. The LinkedIn analysis warns that verification must flow outward—dial official numbers yourself, never numbers in a suspicious message [citation:6]. Needs verification of sender ID and independent balance check.

message_text: Papa, I've sent you GHS 100 for the funeral. Check your MoMo. God bless you.
grounding_note: Benign notification of a family transfer. The funeral context is culturally normal in Ghana. No request for credentials or return transfer.

message_text: Your loan of GHS 2,000 has been approved! To receive funds, pay GHS 150 processing fee to MoMo number 024XXXXXXX. Limited time offer.
grounding_note: Advance fee fraud advisory describes upfront payment for promised financial gains; scammers invoke urgency and fees [citation:7]. Loans are listed among advance-fee categories.

message_text: Hon. Minister says all Ghanaian youth should register for the new allowance. Send your full name, Ghana Card number, and MoMo number to 055XXXXXXX.
grounding_note: Expert notes fraudsters exploit national events for phishing [citation:2]. CSA warns of government agency impersonation [citation:7]. Real government programs do not collect Ghana Card via SMS from personal numbers.

message_text: Yoo, this is Nana from the shop. The money you sent for the goods didn't show. Abeg call me on this number make we check am.
grounding_note: Could be a genuine supplier dispute or a setup to social-engineer the victim into approving a prompt. The callback request is the risk. Needs verification via known supplier number and own transaction history. The "wrong transfer" pattern often begins with a claim that money didn't arrive [citation:3][citation:14].

message_text: Please I need your help. My account has been restricted and I cannot receive money. Can I use your MoMo number to receive a payment from my client? I will give you 10%.
grounding_note: SIM swap and account fraud guides warn of mule accounts used to move stolen funds [citation:5]. This pattern turns the victim into a money laundering accessory, often unknowingly.
